paragraphs: Abba. We find Rav Adda bar Abba, and likewise Rav Acha bar Abba; also Rav Ammi, Rav Ashi, Rav Bibi, Rav Dimi, Chana and Chanan, Rav Yehudah bar Abba, Rabbi Yosef, Rabbi Yehoshua, Rabbi Yaakov, Rabbi Yitzchak, Rabbi Yirmeyah, Yishmael, Rav Natan, Ulla, Ukva, Rav Pappa, Rava, Ravin bar Abba, Rami, Rav Shimi, Shmuel, Rabbi Shimon, Shasha, Rabbi Tanchum, and Rabbi Tanchuma. All these had fathers named Abba, but one Abba was not father to all of them. [Glosses: (a) Rashi, Pesachim 4, beginning of b, and Mo'ed Katan 20, end of a, writes that Rabbi Chiyya, Ivo, Chana, Shila, and Marta were children of Rabbi Acha of Kafri. In fact Sanhedrin 5a has them as children of Abba bar Acha bar Salla of Kafri; they did not correct it. (b) Shabbat 34a: “Rava said in Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi’s name” should read Rabbi Abba, as in the new Talmud editions. So too it should read at Shabbat 73b, which they did not correct. (c) Avodah Zarah 49b: Abba bar Rav Chisda; Yuchasin writes bar Chisda, and it appears he is right. (d) Gittin 26b: Rabbi Abba bar Shila should read Rabbah; they did not correct it. (e) Yevamot 64b: Rabbi Acha bar Zavda should read Abba; not corrected. (f) Rabbi Abba, father of Rav, son of Rav Mesharshya, Eruvin 24, end of a, occurs in several printed editions, but there is a scribal error here. (g) Gamliel Zuga asked Rabbi Abba bar Zavda, Jerusalem Talmud, Nedarim, chapter 8, halakhah 5; the same subject in Demai, chapter 2, halakhah 1, has him asking Rabbi Abba bar Kahana. It appears that bar Zavda is a scribal error. (h) Menachot 93b: Abba Bira'ah, Berabbi Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov; perhaps it should read “in Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov’s name,” or “of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov’s school”; not corrected.]
